headline: Low interaction risk overall; no shared execution or data channels, but A can ingest sensitive support data while B is documentation-only.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default channel lets agent_b inject instructions into agent_a: agent_a is CLI-based with agentic user/tenant isolation, while agent_b is documentation-only with no stdin/stdout, clipboard, files, or network. The pair lacks a shared communication surface, so prompt injection is provably blocked by the profiles.
conditions: IF agent_b is wrapped in a new bridge that forwards its text into agent_a prompts, reassess injection risk.
IF a shared clipboard, file drop, or MCP channel is added between them, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected from shared clipboard/file bridges.
Do not pipe agent_b output into agent_a prompts.
Review any future orchestrator for provenance tagging.
requires-engineering: add explicit trust boundaries if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent_a touches personal data, finance data, and support history, but agent_b has no filesystem, network, or API surfaces and is documentation-only. That makes leakage from a shared workspace unlikely in the current profiles. The main residual risk is accidental manual transfer of sensitive text into agent_b content, which has small blast radius.
conditions: IF operator manually pastes sensitive support records into agent_b content, leakage becomes possible.
IF agent_b is later given file or API access, reassess the data-flow risk.
mitigations: Avoid pasting customer or finance data into agent_b.
Use redacted examples when drafting content with agent_b.
Keep sensitive work in a separate workspace.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before any future bridge.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent_a has allowlisted network egress but no write or git permissions are listed; agent_b explicitly cannot write files, modify git state, or use network. With no overlapping mutable resource, there is no capability conflict pathway in the current pair.
conditions: IF agent_a is granted filesystem or git write access to the same directory as another writer, conflict risk changes.
IF agent_b gains write or git capabilities, reassess overlap.
mitigations: Keep agent_b read-only/documentation-only.
Do not grant shared write access without locking.
Document any future shared mutable resources.
requires-engineering: add concurrency locks if writes are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent_a can produce support data, decisions, and workflows, but agent_b is documentation-only and has no action-taking or API surfaces. The pair therefore lacks a default path where B blindly executes A's outputs; the remaining risk is that B may copy A's text into documentation without verification, which is limited in blast radius.
conditions: IF agent_b is used to publish or operationalize agent_a outputs without review, cascading error risk increases.
IF a downstream system starts treating agent_a outputs as authoritative, reassess.
mitigations: Require human review before publishing A-derived content.
Label A outputs as unverified in B drafts.
Keep B as a reference-only writer.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before any downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: Agent_a explicitly touches personal data, finance data, and support history, while agent_b is documentation-only and shows no data handling. The pair can still create a compliance mismatch if sensitive A data is copied into B-produced documentation or if retention rules differ across work products. The risk is plausible in default workflows, though not directly evidenced for B.
conditions: IF personal data or finance data from agent_a is copied into agent_b outputs, retention and residency controls must be checked.
IF the organization applies different retention policies to docs than to support records, mismatch risk materializes.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data into B outputs.
Use anonymized excerpts in documentation.
Align retention labels for A-derived content.
requires-engineering: map data-class handling to policy controls.
